edition.label: supplied WebToEpub compilation, metadata dated 2022-04-29
edition.qualification: Dossier verified local snapshot/navigation; primary authenticity and publication completeness not certified.

evidence.supports: Comparator only: one narrated stabbing is followed by return to Cirin; Zach reports prior invasion deaths. It does not define an automatic restart for arbitrary killing or the final ritual.

evidence.locator: Ch. 83, OEBPS/Text/0083_83_The_Quiet_Life.xhtml p166-198; Ch. 84, OEBPS/Text/0084_84_Powerless.xhtml p2-18
evidence.supports: Quatach-Ichl detonates his own soul; Zorian initiates the restart before blackout and wakes with severe soul injury still present. This specific initiated restart does not prove an automatic response to arbitrary death.
Final ritual roles, costs, lethal Guardian/primordial threat, Zorian's pre-running soul-exit contingency, possession of his sleeping original, and release of the original soul.
Loop-body anchors fail after return; marker tracking/rescue is costly; Zach needs treatment; Zach reports the outside timeline continued.
Fresh counterparts lack loop relationships; invasion retreats while Sudomir escapes; Jornak suffers a separate actual deadline-pact death after Zach's contract dissolves.

cases.pre_state: Final Festival-alignment breach, Ch. 91. Gate/Guardian, Key, alignment, ritual roles, Orb and costly contributions are relevant; source does not supply a stable universal remaining-iteration count here.
cases.no_intervention: Ritual opens costly path; allies die; Zorian is mortally pierced, executes the prepared soul separation, wins a soul contest for his sleeping original's body and releases the original soul. He then wakes outside the loop; body-anchored enhancements fail and he must spend resources to wake Zach.

hypothetical_outcomes.result: Attempt fails or access is denied during the ritual.
hypothetical_outcomes.basis: Source shows lethal Guardian attack and assigned costly roles, but does not define player access/combat. Failure receipt is an original proposal; no silent interruption.

hypothetical_outcomes.result: Eligible attack kills Zorian before the final-exit contingency.
hypothetical_outcomes.basis: Outcome is unknown. Chapter 91 does not establish a restart, canonical return, player survival, or memory transfer if this contingency is beaten.

hypothetical_outcomes.result: Player removes a required ritual contribution before the path stabilizes.
hypothetical_outcomes.basis: The ritual dependencies are source-evidenced, but every substitution and resulting loop/world state are not. Author the dependency response; do not recreate the canonical exit.

cases.knowledge_and_response: Retain loop memories only through a source-defined marker/memory carrier; originals/counterparts do not inherit relationships by default. Gate roles, collaborators, Guardian, Zach and outside society hold different evidence. Independent surviving actors may change plans when contributors disappear; source gives no universal fallback.

closures.actor: A witnessed death, a character-initiated restart, the special soul-exit/identity transfer, and post-exit death are distinct transitions; arbitrary final-ritual death remains unresolved.
closures.player: Player death/knowledge/return contract is unknown and requires an explicit rule.
closures.society: Outside timeline continues; local invasion and surviving threats resolve on their own state.

evidence.supports: Downstream: Gu removes/subdues the Halberd into private Weapon Space and departs with Liuli and Yan Ji; local observers falsely infer he sealed it; Liuli remains controlled and later reports hazy memories and thoughts of Gu. These are not Ye's return or freely chosen allegiance.

cases.pre_state: Secret-realm arc, physical 59-70. Ye Chen has map/key, ring-bound Yan Ji and a pursuit of the Eight Desolate Demon Halberd. Gu has an undisclosed pill mark, system information, Elder Ming protection, and an independent reason to follow. The entry ceiling is a world rule; 'favored son' is not automatic combat protection.
cases.no_intervention: Gu tracks Ye by the marked pill. Their mistrust severs Yan Ji's bond and costs Ye 200 Fortune; Gu defeats the key attack. He coerces Liuli into opening her Knowledge Sea under an oath she expects to constrain him, plants a different control mechanism, and kills Ye at zero Fortune. Gu claims his demonic nature consumes heavenly demons and avoids backlash. This is a source-specific exception, not transferable player immunity.

hypothetical_outcomes.result: Attempted entry/attack fails or is denied at the realm boundary.
hypothetical_outcomes.basis: Source establishes an above-cap repelling/lethal boundary; does not establish player access or outcome. Surface denial or concrete failed entry rather than protagonist immunity.

hypothetical_outcomes.result: Player reveals pill tracking or protects Liuli's party; Ye escapes the planned confrontation.
hypothetical_outcomes.basis: Original proposal. The source supports the secret mark and party danger, not successful warning, trust, escape, or Gu's fallback. Do not respawn Ye or recreate the same confrontation.

hypothetical_outcomes.result: Canon-supported Gu kills Ye after zero Fortune; alternatively, an authored eligible player kill happens earlier.
hypothetical_outcomes.basis: Gu's actual death/oath exception is supported at physical 69-70. Earlier player death, equivalent threshold reward, oath immunity, loot/identity transfer, and demonic outcome are not supported and must be separately authored.

cases.knowledge_and_response: Ye does not know the pill mark; Gu does. Yan Ji knows the relationship break; Liuli, Aunt Xue, retainers and public rumor have separate views. Future reactions need actual witness/information channels. Gu may act only through retained means/resources; no universal replacement target.

closures.actor: Ye's narrated death is terminal in the reviewed arc; no return is shown. Gu retains the Halberd; Liuli survives with compromised autonomy and later hazy memory; Yan Ji accompanies Gu under explicit perception limits.
closures.player: No transferable Fortune, immunity, title, oath bypass, identity, or power is evidenced.
closures.society: Lower-Realm observers wrongly believe Gu sealed the artifact. Broader political consequences outside reviewed claims are unknown.
